examples.ko: 협회가 발행하는 간행물 목록을 홈페이지에서 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked the list of publications issued by the association on its website.

examples.ko: 사내 간행물에 실을 원고를 이번 주 금요일까지 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please send the manuscript for the company publication by this Friday.
I checked the year of publication at the back of the book.

examples.ko: 협회에서 새 사전의 간행을 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: The association is preparing to publish a new dictionary.

examples.ko: 비용 문제로 잡지의 간행이 계속 늦어지고 있어요.
examples.en: Because of cost problems, the magazine's publication keeps getting delayed.

examples.ko: 이 시집은 간행 후 일주일 만에 다 팔렸어요.
examples.en: This poetry collection sold out within a week of publication.

explain: 책이나 잡지를 만들어 내는 일인데, 일상에서는 '출판'이나 '발행'을 더 많이 말해요. '간행'은 학회, 협회, 오래된 책 이야기에서 보이는 딱딱한 말이에요. '간행물', '간행 연도'처럼 붙여서 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means producing a book or magazine, but in daily life people more often say '출판' or '발행'. 간행 is a stiff word seen with academic societies, associations and old books. It is often used in set combinations like '간행물' and '간행 연도'.

examples.ko: 이 유적은 고고학적 가치가 아주 높아요.
examples.en: This site has very high archaeological value.

examples.ko: 새로운 고고학적 발견 덕분에 옛 마을의 모습을 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a new archaeological discovery, we learned what the old village looked like.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 고고학적 자료를 직접 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see archaeological materials in person at the museum.

examples.ko: 그 섬에서 고고학적 조사가 다시 시작됐어요.
examples.en: Archaeological research has started again on that island.
This place is important from an archaeological point of view as well.

examples.ko: 고고학적 의미가 큰 물건이 땅속에서 나왔어요.
examples.en: An object of great archaeological significance was found underground.

explain: '역사적'은 기록이나 사건 쪽이고, '고고학적'은 땅에서 나온 유물과 유적을 조사하는 쪽이에요. 뒤에 '가치', '조사', '발굴', '자료' 같은 말이 자주 오고, '고고학적인 발견'처럼 '인'을 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: '역사적' (historical) points to records and events, while '고고학적' points to relics and sites dug up from the ground. It often comes before words like '가치', '조사', '발굴' and '자료', and you can also say '고고학적인 발견' with '인'.

examples.en: Competition for high-paying jobs is very fierce.
This industry is famous for high pay.
The more you are paid, the bigger the responsibility.
The factory moved overseas because of high wages.

examples.ko: 고임금 직장에 들어가려고 공부를 열심히 해요.
examples.en: I study hard to get into a well-paying workplace.

examples.ko: 고임금과 저임금의 차이가 점점 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: The gap between high and low wages keeps growing.

explain: 반대말은 '저임금'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '월급이 많다'고 하고, '고임금'은 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '저임금' (low wage). In daily talk people say '월급이 많다', while '고임금' appears more in news and economic discussion.

examples.en: They observe the stars every night at the observatory.

examples.ko: 기상청은 태풍의 움직임을 계속 관측하고 있어요.
examples.en: The weather agency keeps monitoring the typhoon's movement.

examples.ko: 오늘 밤에는 달을 관측하기 좋은 날씨예요.
examples.en: Tonight's weather is good for observing the moon.

examples.ko: 학생들이 비의 양을 직접 관측해서 기록했어요.
examples.en: The students measured the rainfall themselves and recorded it.
Scientists announced that they had observed a new star.

examples.ko: 지진을 관측하는 장치가 산 아래에 있어요.
examples.en: A device that monitors earthquakes is at the foot of the mountain.

explain: '보다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '관측하다'는 별이나 날씨처럼 장비로 자세히 살피고 기록할 때 써요. 사람의 행동이나 분위기를 지켜볼 때는 '관찰하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 보다 is the everyday verb, while 관측하다 is for watching and recording things like stars or weather, usually with instruments. For watching a person's behavior or mood, 관찰하다 is more natural.

examples.ko: 이 실험 결과는 기존 이론을 반증해요.
examples.en: This experiment's result disproves the existing theory.

examples.ko: 그 주장을 반증할 자료를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for data that can refute that claim.

examples.ko: 새 연구가 예전 가설을 반증했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a new study disproved the earlier hypothesis.

examples.ko: 그 말을 반증하려면 확실한 증거가 필요해요.
examples.en: To disprove that statement, you need solid evidence.

examples.ko: 상대 의견을 반증하지 못하면 설득력이 없어요.
examples.en: If you can't refute the other side's opinion, it isn't persuasive.

examples.ko: 과학자들은 서로의 주장을 반증하며 발전해 왔어요.
examples.en: Scientists have advanced by disproving each other's claims.

explain: '반박하다'는 말로 맞서 주장하는 것이고, '반증하다'는 반대되는 증거로 어떤 주장이 틀렸음을 보여 주는 거예요. 반대로 맞다는 것을 보이는 말은 '입증하다, 증명하다'예요. 논문이나 토론에서 주로 쓰고 명사 '반증'도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '반박하다' is arguing back in words, while '반증하다' is showing a claim is wrong by presenting contrary evidence. The opposite, showing something is true, is '입증하다' or '증명하다'. It is used mostly in papers and debates, and the noun '반증' is common too.

examples.en: My father is a blue-collar worker who works at a factory.

examples.ko: 블루칼라와 화이트칼라의 월급 차이가 줄고 있대요.
examples.en: I heard the pay gap between blue-collar and white-collar workers is shrinking.
These days blue-collar jobs have become popular too.

examples.ko: 블루칼라는 주로 몸을 쓰는 일을 한다고 해요.
examples.en: Blue-collar workers are said to mainly do physical work.

examples.ko: 대학을 안 나왔다고 블루칼라로 보는 건 편견이에요.
examples.en: Seeing someone as blue-collar just because they did not attend university is a prejudice.

examples.ko: 저는 블루칼라 직종에서 십 년을 일했어요.
examples.en: I have worked in a blue-collar job for ten years.

explain: 짝말은 '화이트칼라'이고, 뉴스나 사회 이야기에서 직업 종류를 나눌 때 나와요. 일상에서는 '생산직', '현장직'이라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '화이트칼라', and it appears in news and social discussions when dividing types of jobs. In daily speech people also say '생산직' or '현장직'.

examples.en: The teacher explained the rules in detail.
Please tell me the details of the accident.
I read the contract carefully before signing.

examples.ko: 여행 일정은 메일로 상세히 보내 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll send the travel schedule in detail by email.

examples.ko: 의사가 약 먹는 방법을 상세히 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me how to take the medicine in detail.
I want to know the results in more detail.

explain: 상세히는 빠짐없이 자세하게 한다는 느낌이에요. 같은 뜻의 '자세히'는 말할 때 훨씬 자연스럽고, 상세히는 설명서, 뉴스, 회사 문서 같은 격식 있는 자리에서 잘 써요. 반대로 간단하게 하는 건 '간단히'나 '대충'이에요.
explain_en: 상세히 gives the feeling of leaving nothing out. 자세히 means the same and is much more natural in speech, while 상세히 fits formal places like manuals, news, and company documents. The opposite is doing it briefly: 간단히 or 대충.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 반도체 연구소에서 신소재를 연구해요.
examples.en: My friend researches new materials at a semiconductor lab.
This bag is made of a lightweight new material.

examples.ko: 신소재 덕분에 옷이 더 얇고 따뜻해졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to a new material, the clothes became thinner and warmer.
I saw news that they succeeded in developing a new material.
New materials are also used in cars.
I want to major in materials engineering at university.

explain: 새로 개발된 소재를 말하고, 뉴스나 광고에서 자주 나와요. '소재'는 만드는 데 쓰는 재료라서 '재료'와 비슷하지만, '신소재'는 특별히 새 기술로 만든 것이라는 느낌이 있어요. 대학 학과 이름에도 많이 쓰여요.
explain_en: It refers to a newly developed material and is common in news and advertising. '소재' is close to '재료', but '신소재' suggests something made with new technology. It is also widely used in university department names.

en: to be substantiated; to be demonstrated

examples.en: That theory was proven by experiment.

examples.ko: 효과가 실증되기 전에는 판매할 수 없어요.
examples.en: It can't be sold until its effect is proven.

examples.ko: 이 방법의 안전성이 여러 번 실증됐어요.
examples.en: The safety of this method has been demonstrated many times.

examples.ko: 가설이 실증되면 논문을 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the hypothesis is proven, I can write a paper.
I included only proven facts in the report.
The medicine's effect hasn't been proven yet.

explain: 추측이 아니라 실험이나 자료 같은 실제 증거로 확인된다는 느낌이에요. 논문, 뉴스, 연구 이야기에 주로 나오고 일상 대화에서는 '증명되다'나 '확인되다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It stresses being confirmed by real evidence such as experiments or data, not by guesswork. It appears mostly in papers, news, and research talk; in daily speech people prefer 증명되다 or 확인되다.

en: to be verified; to be demonstrated

examples.en: It was proven that what he said is true.
This medicine's effect is proven by experiments.
If his innocence is proven, he'll be released right away.

examples.ko: 아직 입증되지 않은 이야기는 믿지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't believe stories that haven't been proven yet.

examples.ko: 연구를 통해 운동이 기억력에 좋다는 것이 입증되었어요.
examples.en: Research has shown that exercise is good for memory.
He's a player whose skill has been proven, so everyone expects a lot.

explain: '증명되다'와 비슷하지만 법정, 연구, 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 수학 문제는 '증명하다', 사실이나 효과, 실력은 '입증하다'를 써요. 반대로 '입증되지 않았다'는 아직 확인이 안 됐다는 말이에요. 능동형은 '입증하다'예요.
explain_en: It is similar to 증명되다 and is often used in courtrooms, research, and news. Math is 증명하다, while facts, effects, and ability are 입증하다. '입증되지 않았다' means it has not been confirmed yet. The active form is 입증하다.

p.n: 입증 is common for evidence in law and research; 증명 is more general.

examples.en: My father subscribes to an architecture trade magazine.
This article was published in a medical journal.

examples.ko: 전문지에는 일반 잡지보다 어려운 말이 많아요.
examples.en: Specialist magazines have more difficult words than general ones.

examples.ko: 전문지 기자로 일한 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been five years since I started as a trade magazine reporter.

examples.ko: 그 분야 전문지를 읽으면 최신 소식을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: Reading that field's trade magazine tells you the latest news.

examples.ko: 전문지에 글을 실으려면 심사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: To publish in a specialist magazine, you must pass a review.

explain: 앞에 분야 이름을 붙여서 '의학 전문지', '컴퓨터 전문지'라고 해요. 여러 분야를 다루는 신문은 '종합지'라고 해서 짝이 돼요. 그 일을 하는 사람이 많이 읽어서 말이 조금 어려워요.
explain_en: Put the field before it: '의학 전문지', '컴퓨터 전문지'. Its counterpart is '종합지', which covers many fields. Readers are mostly people in that line of work, so the language is a little harder.

examples.en: My uncle works in the politics desk of a newspaper.
A politics reporter delivered the news from the National Assembly.
I want to work in the society desk rather than the politics desk.
The broadcaster's politics desk got busy from dawn.
A reporter from the politics desk published a book.

examples.ko: 정치부 기사는 뉴스 맨 앞에 나올 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Politics desk stories often come at the front of the news.

explain: 신문사나 방송국에서 정치 소식을 맡는 부서예요. 다른 부서로는 '사회부', '경제부', '문화부', '스포츠부'가 있어요. 뒤에 '기자'를 붙여 '정치부 기자'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: The department at a newspaper or broadcaster that covers political news. Other desks include 사회부, 경제부, 문화부 and 스포츠부. It is often used before 기자, as in 정치부 기자.

examples.en: Try finding the minimum value in this graph.
Today's minimum temperature was five degrees below zero.
Please calculate what the minimum value is.

examples.ko: 최솟값보다 작은 수는 입력할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't enter a number smaller than the minimum value.
Find the difference between the minimum and maximum values.
I wrote code that finds the minimum value in an array.

explain: 반대말은 '최댓값'이고, 수학이나 통계, 프로그래밍 수업에서 많이 나와요. 맞춤법으로는 사이시옷을 넣어 '최솟값'으로 적어요. 일상에서는 '가장 작은 값'이라고 풀어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '최댓값', and it appears often in math, statistics and programming classes. The standard spelling includes the sai-siot, '최솟값'. In everyday talk people may say '가장 작은 값' instead.

examples.en: Metal was detected at the airport security check.
A strange signal was picked up on the radar.
When smoke is detected, an alarm sounds.
The rescue team set out for the detected location.
I was relieved because no virus was detected.

examples.ko: 소리가 너무 작아 탐지될 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The sound was too faint to be detected.

explain: 숨어 있거나 잘 안 보이는 것을 기계나 장치가 찾아낼 때 써요. 사람이 눈으로 찾을 때는 '발견되다'가 자연스러워요. 능동은 '탐지하다'이고, '탐지기', '탐지견'처럼 다른 말과 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a machine or device finds something hidden or hard to see. When a person finds something by eye, '발견되다' sounds more natural. The active form is '탐지하다', and it also joins other words, as in '탐지기' (detector) and '탐지견' (detection dog).

en: to be written; to be marked

examples.en: The price is marked next to the product.
The name is written in both Hangul and English.
The expiration date is printed on the back of the package.

examples.ko: 지도에 표기된 길로 갔더니 공원이 나왔어요.
examples.en: I took the route marked on the map and came to a park.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 발음과 다르게 표기될 때가 많아요.
examples.en: This word is often spelled differently from how it sounds.
The country of origin was written so small that it was hard to check.

explain: '쓰여 있다'보다 딱딱하고, 포장지, 지도, 안내문에 정해진 방식으로 적혀 있을 때 써요. '한글 표기', '영어 표기'처럼 명사 '표기'도 자주 나와요. 직접 손으로 쓰는 일에는 '쓰다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than 쓰여 있다 and fits things shown in a set way on packaging, maps, or notices. The noun 표기, as in 한글 표기, is also common. For writing by hand, 쓰다 sounds more natural.

dis.h: shown by label or spelling notation

p.n: Shown as a label versus written down.
